done_when: Find the root cause of each (Forge not waiting for its processes to exit, or the test checking too early or on a reused id) and fix it at the cause; both tests pass on every OS in CI three runs in a row; no test is skipped or loosened to pass

findings.body: The added case makes `test_6_nothing_left_running` fail on Linux on days 1–9 of each month. It records raw `ps("lstart")` output, whose day is space-padded (for example, `Oct  1`; see the [procps implementation](https://gitlab.com/procps-ng/procps/-/raw/master/src/ps/output.c)). However, `identity()` at src/forge/codex.py:319–320 collapses internal whitespace. The timestamps therefore differ, doctor treats the live driver as a different process, and the assertion at test line 319 fails. Normalize the recorded timestamp consistently so the fix does not introduce another recurring CI failure.

findings.body: A zombie retains its PID and start time, so this comparison now returns True after termination. [Linux distinguishes termination from reaping](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/wait.2.html). This makes `_stop` at src/forge/codex.py:373–376 exhaust both polling periods; in the driver timeout path, reaping cannot happen until `_stop_leftover` returns (lines 241–245). An unreaped lock owner also prevents doctor from recovering leftovers because `_take` at lines 408–410 treats it as active. Check process state while preserving identity across exec. The added test misses this defect: `_down` independently excludes zombies at tests/test_codex_record.py:110–125, and its doctor assertion permits an additional warning that the process still runs.
findings.title: Exclude terminated, unreaped processes from the alive check

why: Main's CI is red on and off: tests/test_codex_record.py::test_6_nothing_left_running fails on macOS and Linux (_down(pid) is False right after the stop), and tests/test_codex_reader.py::test_10_the_cold_read_runs_on_the_other_family fails on Linux (forge doctor doesn't report stopping a crashed forge read's processes), so every pull request hits them
